- grep for "markdown" or "Markdown" or "Parser" in the service layer
- Check if there's an interface for markdown processing and its implementations

Read each file carefully and provide exact answers with file paths and line numbers.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). 14	// Profile is the configuration to start main server.
15	type Profile struct {
16		// Demo indicates if the server is in demo mode
17		Demo bool
18		// Addr is the binding address for server
19		Addr string
20		// Port is the binding port for server
21		Port int
22		// UNIXSock is the IPC binding path. Overrides Addr and Port
23		UNIXSock string
24		// Data is the data directory
25		Data string
26		// DSN points to where memos stores its own data
27		DSN string
28		// Driver is the database driver
29		// sqlite, mysql
30		Driver string
31		// Version is the current version of server
32		Version string
33		// Commit is the current build commit of server
34		Commit string
35		// InstanceURL is the url of your memos instance.
36		InstanceURL string
37	}
38	
39	// AllowAnonymous reports whether unauthenticated visitors may access the instance.
40	//
41	// Anonymous access is enabled only when an InstanceURL is configured. An instance
42	// with no InstanceURL set is treated as private: anonymous callers are limited to
43	// the auth-bootstrap endpoints (sign-in, share links, etc.) and the web UI redirects
44	// them to the sign-in page instead of the public Explore view. Authenticated callers
45	// (session, access token, or personal access token) are never affected.
46	func (p *Profile) AllowAnonymous() bool {
47		return strings.TrimSpace(p.InstanceURL) != ""
48	}
49	
50	func checkDataDir(dataDir string) (string, error) {
51		// Convert to absolute path if relative path is supplied.
52		if !filepath.IsAbs(dataDir) {
53			// Use current working directory, not the binary's directory
54			// This ensures we use the actual working directory where the process runs
55			absDir, err := filepath.Abs(dataDir)
56			if err != nil {
57				return "", err
58			}
59			dataDir = absDir
60		}
61	
62		// Trim trailing \ or / in case user supplies
63		dataDir = strings.TrimRight(dataDir, "\\/")
64		if _, err := os.Stat(dataDir); err != nil {
65			return "", errors.Wrapf(err, "unable to access data folder %s", dataDir)
66		}
67		return dataDir, nil
68	}
69	
70	func (p *Profile) Validate() error {
71		// Set default data directory if not specified
72		if p.Data == "" {
73			if runtime.GOOS == "windows" {
74				p.Data = filepath.Join(os.Getenv("ProgramData"), "memos")
75			} else {
76				// On Linux/macOS, check if /var/opt/memos exists and is writable (Docker scenario)
77				if info, err := os.Stat("/var/opt/memos"); err == nil && info.IsDir() {
78					// Check if we can write to this directory
79					testFile := filepath.Join("/var/opt/memos", ".write-test")
80					if err := os.WriteFile(testFile, []byte("test"), 0600); err == nil {
81						os.Remove(testFile)
82						p.Data = "/var/opt/memos"
83					} else {
84						// /var/opt/memos exists but is not writable, use current directory
85						slog.Warn("/var/opt/memos is not writable, using current directory")
86						p.Data = "."
87					}
88				} else {
89					// /var/opt/memos doesn't exist, use current directory (local development)
90					p.Data = "."
91				}
92			}
93		}
94	
95		// Create data directory if it doesn't exist
96		if _, err := os.Stat(p.Data); os.IsNotExist(err) {
97			if err := os.MkdirAll(p.Data, 0770); err != nil {
98				slog.Error("failed to create data directory", slog.String("data", p.Data), slog.String("error", err.Error()))
99				return err
100			}
101		}
102	
103		dataDir, err := checkDataDir(p.Data)
104		if err != nil {
105			slog.Error("failed to check dsn", slog.String("data", dataDir), slog.String("error", err.Error()))
106			return err
107		}
108	
109		p.Data = dataDir
110		if p.Driver == "sqlite" && p.DSN == "" {
111			mode := "prod"
112			if p.Demo {
113				mode = "demo"
114			}
115			dbFile := fmt.Sprintf("memos_%s.db", mode)
116			p.DSN = filepath.Join(dataDir, dbFile)
117		}
118	
119		return nil
120	}

65	func (s *APIV1Service) RegisterGateway(ctx context.Context, echoServer *echo.Echo) error {
66		// Shared authorizer: one source of truth for authentication and anonymous-access
67		// policy, used by both the gRPC-Gateway middleware and the Connect interceptor.
68		authorizer := NewAuthorizer(s.Store, s.Secret, s.Profile)
69		gatewayAuthMiddleware := func(next runtime.HandlerFunc) runtime.HandlerFunc {
70			return func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, pathParams map[string]string) {
71				ctx := r.Context()
72	
73				// The RPC method name is set by grpc-gateway after routing. When it can't be
74				// determined, skip the policy check and let the service layer handle visibility.
75				rpcMethod, ok := runtime.RPCMethod(ctx)
76				authHeader := r.Header.Get("Authorization")
77	
78				result := authorizer.Authenticate(ctx, authHeader)
79				if ok {
80					if err := authorizer.CheckAccess(ctx, rpcMethod, result); err != nil {
81						http.Error(w, `{"code": 16, "message": "authentication required"}`, http.StatusUnauthorized)
82						return
83					}
84				}
85	
86				// Apply the identity to the context (no-op for permitted anonymous requests).
87				if result != nil {
88					r = r.WithContext(auth.ApplyToContext(ctx, result))
89				}
90	
91				next(w, r, pathParams)
92			}
93		}
94	
95		// Create gRPC-Gateway mux with auth middleware.
96		gwMux := runtime.NewServeMux(
97			runtime.WithMiddlewares(gatewayAuthMiddleware),
98		)
99		if err := v1pb.RegisterInstanceServiceHandlerServer(ctx, gwMux, s); err != nil {
100			return err
101		}
102		if err := v1pb.RegisterAuthServiceHandlerServer(ctx, gwMux, s); err != nil {
103			return err
104		}
105		if err := v1pb.RegisterUserServiceHandlerServer(ctx, gwMux, s); err != nil {
106			return err
107		}
108		if err := v1pb.RegisterMemoServiceHandlerServer(ctx, gwMux, s); err != nil {
109			return err
110		}
111		if err := v1pb.RegisterAttachmentServiceHandlerServer(ctx, gwMux, s); err != nil {
112			return err
113		}
114		if err := v1pb.RegisterAIServiceHandlerServer(ctx, gwMux, s); err != nil {
115			return err
116		}
117		if err := v1pb.RegisterShortcutServiceHandlerServer(ctx, gwMux, s); err != nil {
118			return err
119		}
120		if err := v1pb.RegisterIdentityProviderServiceHandlerServer(ctx, gwMux, s); err != nil {
121			return err
122		}
123		gwGroup := echoServer.Group("")
124		// Register SSE endpoint with same CORS as rest of /api/v1.
125		RegisterSSERoutes(gwGroup, s.SSEHub, s.Store, s.Secret)
126		handler := echo.WrapHandler(http.MaxBytesHandler(gwMux, maxAPIRequestBytes))
127	
128		gwGroup.Any("/api/v1/*", handler)
129		gwGroup.Any("/file/*", handler)
130	
131		// Connect handlers for browser clients (replaces grpc-web).
132		logStacktraces := s.Profile.Demo
133		connectInterceptors := connect.WithInterceptors(
134			NewMetadataInterceptor(), // Convert HTTP headers to gRPC metadata first
135			NewLoggingInterceptor(logStacktraces),
136			NewRecoveryInterceptor(logStacktraces),
137			NewAuthInterceptor(authorizer),
138		)
139		connectMux := http.NewServeMux()
140		connectHandler := NewConnectServiceHandler(s)
141		connectHandler.RegisterConnectHandlers(connectMux, connectInterceptors, connect.WithReadMaxBytes(maxAPIRequestBytes))
142	
143		connectGroup := echoServer.Group("")
144		connectGroup.Any("/memos.api.v1.*", echo.WrapHandler(http.MaxBytesHandler(connectMux, maxAPIRequestBytes)))
145	
146		return nil
147	}
